direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is good, as it is what you would expect from over-the-top, 'Rube Goldberg' death sequences you would see from this franchise, done well with a larger budget; The direction on a microscale is pretty bad, as it is very obvious none of the budget went into the acting; The storytelling is pretty straightforward; The tension is pretty forced, especially considering you know there is going to be a death sequence when they switch to the IMAX sequences, but it is still decent and makes you feel uneasy

performance.comments: The only performance that is passable as you can see some range, and the fact that she cares about what is going on
Really more of a cameo, but he plays his final role in the franchise well as he rides off into the sunset

cast.comments: It is very obvious that none of the budget went into the acting, as many of these performances are from inexperienced, no-name actors

story.comments: The concept is decent, especially for a Final Destination movie, as the movie takes the Final Destination concept and adds some depth to it by sharing how the bloodlines come into the picture; The plot structure is pretty straightforward, especially considering the conflict naturally progresses the story forward, but the exposition and resolution feel very disjointed from the rest of the movie; There are many plot holes in the movie that are explained with, "just cause"; The character writing is not that great because I really didn't care for any of these characters

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very over-the-top and unnatural; The humor is forced, but not too bad; The foreshadowing is actually good, as they do leave clues and roots that help progress the story and give an idea of how storylines will end, but there are also a good amount of intentional red herrings; It gets messy when they go down this route

cinematography.comments: Uses IMAX surprisingly well, as the action sequences are well-shot and effectively use the technology; Considering every death scene is shot in IMAX, this kind of ruins the surprise because you know there might be a death sequence, even though there are some red herrings

editing.comments: Pretty choppy and poorly put together

sound.comments: Help build tension and create over-the-top death sequences

visual_effects.comments: Uses this well to help create the death sequences, as the 'Rube Goldberg' death sequences are very over-the-top and true to the franchise; the movie uses its fifty-million-dollar budget well to help create these sequences; though it is very obvious when they use CGI, as it is very over-the-top in creating deaths

production_design.comments: The opening restaurant setting was well designed but the rest just looks like the Pacific Northwest

makeup.comments: A little corny and obviously fake;

review.pacing: Pacing is a bit on the slower side as 5–10 minutes could have been cut, but nothing major
review.climax: Climax is executed well as the movie literally goes up in a ball of fire; but the resolution feels disjointed and forced
review.tone: The tone is very over-the-top and traditional to the *Final Destination* franchise;
review.final_notes: The opening sequence for the movie is literally just "Drop" from earlier this year, except if it were shot like "Final Destination"
review.overall: Overall, an entertaining movie that is very true to the *Final Destination* franchise with its over-the-top, Rube Goldberg-like death sequences; but it is also true to the "Final Destination" franchise in that it is filled with bad acting and corny dialogue; it was very obvious all of the budget went into the visual effects and death sequences
